meta.description: Engineering term glossary for EngCalcs translation prompts. Preferred translations per language to prevent term drift across calculators and sprints. Covers all calculators including Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Micro-Hydro Power, and Manning series.
meta.usage: Inject relevant entries as context in translation prompts: 'Use these preferred translations for technical terms: [terms for this calculator prefix]'. Entries with empty strings need a sprint to fill.
meta.confidence_notes: Translations marked with (?) in comments need native-speaker review. am/bn/km/my/ps translations are AI-generated (2026-06) and benefit from native-speaker review before high-stakes use. New entries added 2026-06: rock chute, chute, unit discharge, median rock size (D50), gradation, porosity, specific gravity, ponding, junction loss, run-of-river, headworks. Pre-2026 Spanish translations were done by a non-native, non-engineer speaker — treat as a useful baseline but not authoritative.

wmo-385.title: International Glossary of Hydrology
wmo-385.note: Free PDF. Covers English, French, Russian, Spanish. ~1800 hydrological and hydraulic terms. Primary citation source for es and fr translations.

iate.title: Interactive Terminology for Europe
iate.note: Free, searchable online. Covers all 24 EU official languages. Best source for bg, cs, de, hr, it, pt, ro from our language set.

unterm.title: United Nations Terminology Portal
unterm.note: Free, searchable online. Covers the 6 UN official languages. Best free source for ar and zh.

fao-irrigation.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Papers
fao-irrigation.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
fao-irrigation.note: Free PDF downloads. Applied irrigation/drainage engineering — closer domain match than WMO for emitter, seepage, conveyance efficiency, application rate.

human-pre2026.title: Pre-2026 Human Translations (git history)
human-pre2026.contributor: Tom Haws (es, overall); 'Plamen' (bg, partial, 2020); anonymous contributors (sr, hr, tr, 2013–2020)
human-pre2026.coverage: Calculators available before 2026: Manning Pipe Flow, Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Weir Flow. Not all terms exist for all languages.
human-pre2026.caveat: Tom is a non-native, non-engineering Spanish speaker — es baseline is useful but not authoritative. Pre-2026 sr/hr translations appear to be from a native South Slavic engineering speaker and are considered reliable for the terms covered.
human-pre2026.how_to_access: git show 2ea96c2:lib/lang.ec.sr.php (or hr, bg, tr, es, etc.) — commit 2ea96c2 is the last pre-AI-sprint commit (approx. 2020-05-04)

meta.source_values: wmo-385 (directly cited from WMO No. 385), wmo-385-indirect (inferred from WMO context), iate (cited from IATE), unterm (cited from UNTERM), human-pre2026 (pre-2026 human translation — see bibliography for per-language caveats), ai-generated (no authoritative citation)

terms.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
terms.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg OPEN QUESTION (2026-07): native engineer corrected 'дебит' to 'водно количество' in hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings (rc_, or_). Whether to replace 'дебит' suite-wide (incl. pipes/irrigation) is pending their clarification; keep 'дебит' elsewhere until answered. ENGINEER CLARIFICATION (2026-07-06): 'дебит is a typical colloquial call of the word — regular people and non-hydraulic engineers use it. In university (hydraulic engineering) they used водно количество for Q, never дебит. I guess both work.' So both are acceptable; водно количество is the academic/hydraulic-engineering register, дебит the general register. Still an open decision whether to standardize on водно количество suite-wide.

translations.km: លំហូរ

terms.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
terms.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

translations.km: ល្បឿន
translations.my: ရေအလျင်နှုန်း

terms.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
terms.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred.

translations.km: ការបាត់បង់ថ្ពល

terms.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
terms.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms.

translations.km: កាំធារ
translations.my: ဟိုက်ဒရောလစ်အချင်းဝက်

terms.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
terms.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use.

translations.km: បរិវេណសើម
translations.my: ရေစိုပတ်လည်ဘောင်

terms.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
terms.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'.

translations.km: ភាពក្រញ៉ោងម៉ាន់នីង
translations.my: မန်းနင်းကြမ်းတမ်းမှုကိန်း

terms.context: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor. Dimensionless coefficient in the Darcy-Weisbach head loss equation. Distinct from Hazen-Williams C coefficient.
terms.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term. In some languages, 'friction' and 'resistance' terms compete — prefer 'friction' to match the Darcy-Weisbach naming convention.

translations.km: កត្តាស្ទះ
translations.my: ပွတ်တိုက်မှုကိန်း

terms.context: Coefficient correcting theoretical orifice or weir flow for real-world contraction and friction effects. Appears in Orifice and Weir calculators.
terms.translation_notes: The 'discharge' here refers to flow rate, not the verb. Use the hydraulic engineering compound term.

translations.km: ស្ថេរភាពលំហូរ
translations.my: ရေထွက်ကိန်း

terms.context: A flow-measurement or water-control structure — a barrier across a channel over which water flows. Appears in Weir Flow Simple and Weir Flow Irregular calculators.
terms.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1665 confirms: es = 'vertedero', fr = 'déversoir', ru = 'водослив'. In an irrigation context, the term often overlaps with 'diversion dam' or 'check structure'. Use the term most common among irrigation field workers in the target language, not a purely civil-engineering dictionary term.

translations.km: ស្ទីង
translations.my: တမံ

terms.context: A submerged or free-flowing opening through which water discharges under head. Appears in Orifice Flow and Orifice Drain Time calculators.
terms.translation_notes: In irrigation contexts, often the opening of a headgate or pipe turnout. Use the hydraulic engineering term, not a general word for 'hole' or 'opening'.

translations.km: ប្រហោងទឹក
translations.my: ဂေါက်ဝ

terms.context: Angular rock placed to resist erosion on channel beds and banks. Appears in Manning Trapezoidal Channel and Rock Chute calculators.
terms.translation_notes: No direct single-word equivalent in most languages. Use the established local engineering term — this varies significantly by country. In Spanish, 'enrocado' (general) or 'escollera' (bank protection) are both used; lead with 'enrocado'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg: 'каменна облицовка' (stone lining), not 'каменна наброска'.

translations.km: ថ្មការពារ

terms.context: Ratio of outflow to inflow in a canal reach — measures how much water delivered at the head is received at the tail. Appears in Canal Seepage calculator. E_c = Q_out / Q_in.
terms.translation_notes: This is the most terminology-sensitive term in the suite. 'Conveyance' means transport of water along a canal — do not use a general word for 'efficiency' alone. The term should convey 'how well the canal transports water without loss'.

translations.km: ប្រសិទ្ធភាពដឹកជញ្ជូន
translations.my: ရေသယ်ပို့ထိရောက်မှု

terms.context: Water lost from a canal through the bed and banks by percolation into the soil. Appears in Canal Seepage calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the irrigation/canal engineering term for slow percolation loss, not a word implying leakage through a crack or structural failure.

translations.km: ការជ្រាបទឹក
translations.my: ရေစိမ့်ဆင်းမှု

terms.context: Pressure pipe carrying water from a reservoir or headpond down to a turbine in a micro-hydro system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
terms.translation_notes: 'Penstock' is a specialized term with no exact one-word equivalent in many languages. Use the established civil/hydro engineering phrase for 'pressure conduit' or 'force main to turbine'. Czech: 'tlakovod' (pressure main) is preferred over the generic 'přiváděcí potrubí' (supply pipe). Serbian: 'напорни цевовод' is the standard hydraulic engineering term.

translations.km: បំពង់សម្ពាធ
translations.my: ဖိအားရေပိုက်

terms.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
terms.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

translations.km: ថ្ពល់សរុប
translations.my: စုစုပေါင်းဖိမြင့်ဆင့်

terms.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
terms.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

translations.km: ថ្ពល់សុទ្ធ
translations.my: အသားတင်ဖိမြင့်ဆင့်

terms.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
terms.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency.

translations.km: ប្រសិទ្ធភាពរោងចក្រ
translations.my: စက်ရုံထိရောက်မှု

terms.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file).

translations.km: ឯកសណ្ឋានភាពចែកចាយ

terms.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
terms.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation.

translations.km: អត្រាដាក់ទឹក

terms.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers.

translations.km: ឧបករណ៍ចំណោចទឹក
translations.my: ရေထုတ်ကိရိယာ

terms.context: Water surface elevation on the upstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Weir Flow and Orifice calculators.
terms.translation_notes: 'Headwater' is an upstream water surface — do not confuse with 'head' (energy) or 'source' (origin of a stream). Use the hydraulic structure term.

translations.bg: ниво на вода нагоре по течение
translations.km: កម្ពស់ទឹកខាងលើ
translations.my: ရေတက်ဘက်ရေမြင့်ဆင့်

terms.context: Water surface elevation on the downstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Orifice Flow calculator. When tailwater is above the invert, the orifice is submerged.
terms.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic structure term for downstream water level. Pair consistently with 'headwater elevation'.

translations.bg: ниво на вода надолу по течение
translations.km: កម្ពស់ទឹកខាងក្រោម
translations.my: ရေဆင်းဘက်ရေမြင့်ဆင့်

terms.context: Elevation of the bottom (inside bottom) of a pipe, culvert, or opening. Appears in Orifice Flow and Orifice Drain Time calculators.
terms.translation_notes: 'Invert' is a civil/hydraulic engineering term for the lowest interior point of a conduit or opening. Use the established local term — in many languages this is a direct borrowing or a 'pipe bottom elevation' phrase.

translations.km: កម្ពស់គល់បំពង

terms.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.
terms.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

translations.km: ជម្រាល

terms.context: Flow regime in which fluid moves in parallel layers with no lateral mixing. Reynolds number below ~2000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
terms.translation_notes: Nearly always a direct cognate or borrowing from the Latin in technical languages. Confirm the local engineering convention.

translations.km: ស្រទប់
translations.my: ညီညာသောစီးဆင်းမှု

terms.context: Flow regime with chaotic, irregular mixing. Reynolds number above ~4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
terms.translation_notes: Nearly always a cognate. Some languages distinguish 'turbulent' (adjective) from 'turbulence' (noun) — use the adjective form.

translations.km: រញ្ជួយ
translations.my: ဆူပူသောစီးဆင်းမှု

terms.context: Flow regime between laminar and turbulent — Reynolds number roughly 2000–4000. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach calculator flow regime check.
terms.translation_notes: Use the adjective form meaning 'between two states'. Some languages use 'critical flow' for this regime — check local hydraulics convention.

translations.km: ផ្លាស់ប្ដូរ
translations.my: အကူးအပြောင်းစီးဆင်းမှု

terms.context: A steep rock-lined drop structure (also called a 'rock ramp') that conveys water rapidly down a slope in irrigation, drainage, or watershed management. Key concepts for translation: rock-lined, steep gradient, spillway or drop structure — translate the concept, not the English word 'chute'. The rock riprap matrix dissipates energy and resists erosion. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson) and Robinson Rock Chute calculators.
terms.translation_notes: CRITICAL: 'Robinson' is the surname of K.M. Robinson, co-author of Robinson, Rice & Kadavy (1998) — it is a proper noun and must NEVER be translated or modified in any language. Translate only 'Rock Chute'. Concept to translate: 'rock-lined steep channel' or 'rock-lined spillway' — the drop/descent nature must be conveyed; a generic 'rock channel' is insufficient. CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 establishes that the French word 'chute' means 'fall' (elevation difference) — it cannot name this structure. Use 'coursier en enrochement' (coursier = steep channel structure; enrochement = riprap). Spanish: USDA uses 'bajante de rocado' — 'bajante' (from bajar = to descend) correctly conveys the drop-structure nature; 'de rocado' = rock-lined. Russian: 'каменный быстроток' ('быстроток' = fast-flow/steep channel). Portuguese: changed from 'calha' (generic trough) to 'rampa em enrocamento' (rampa = ramp/slope, enrocamento = riprap) to convey steep character. Serbian: changed from 'жлеб' (gutter/trough) to 'брзоток' (fast-flow structure), consistent with ru/uk pattern. Bengali: changed from borrowed 'চ্যুট' (conveys nothing) to 'পাথর-আবৃত খাড়া নালা' (rock-lined steep channel). Persian: changed from generic 'آبراه سنگی' (stone waterway) to 'آبراه تند سنگچین' (تند = steep/swift, سنگچین = stone-laid/riprap). Pashto: added 'تند' (steep/swift) to original. Khmer: changed 'ចំហ' (open) to 'ជម្រាល' (sloped/inclined). NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: am (ምቀጫ meaning uncertain), my (ထောင် may not clearly convey steep to all readers), de (Steinschütte is standard engineering term but doesn't explicitly say 'steep channel'). Turkish: changed to 'taş düşü' — 'düşü' is the established Turkish hydraulics term for a drop/chute structure (2026-07 audit; previous 'taş eğimli kanal' was descriptive but nonstandard). Spanish: NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION — 'bajante de rocado' claims a USDA source but 'rocado' is not standard Spanish ('enrocado' is); verify the USDA document or switch to 'bajante de enrocado'. 2026-07 reconciliation: fr/ro/ru/uk lang files updated to match this entry. NOT reconciled pending human review of the GLOSSARY side: hr 'kameni skluz' (consider 'kameni brzotok', parallel to sr/ru), bg 'каменна бързина' (consider 'каменен бързоток'), de 'Steinschütte' vs shipped 'Steingerinne' (both defensible - pick one). RESOLVED bg: native Bulgarian engineer confirmed 'каменен бързоток' (2026-07); lang file updated.

translations.km: ប្រឡាយថ្មជម្រាល

terms.context: A steep open channel or drop structure for conveying water rapidly down a slope. Distinct from a gentle-slope irrigation canal. Per ec_lang_intent guidance: translate as 'steep channel' or 'spillway' — not as the word 'chute' borrowed into another language. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Manning Trapezoidal Channel, and related drop-structure calculators.
terms.translation_notes: CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 defines the English word 'fall' (elevation difference) as French 'chute', Spanish 'caída', and Russian 'падение'. The same pattern holds in all three WMO languages: the word for 'fall' (elevation difference) is NOT available for this hydraulic structure. 'Coursier' is the correct French term for the structure. Spanish: 'canal rápido'. Russian: 'быстроток' (the steep channel structure — distinct from 'падение' which means elevation fall). Chinese: '陡槽'.

translations.km: ប្រឡាយលំហូរខ្លាំង
translations.my: မြန်ဆန်သောချောင်း

terms.context: Flow rate per unit width of channel (Q/B), in m²/s or ft²/s. The primary design input for the Robinson rock chute method. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic engineering term. 'Unit' here means 'per unit channel width' — not related to measurement units. Spanish: 'caudal unitario'. French: 'débit unitaire'. German: 'spezifischer Abfluss'. Russian: 'удельный расход'. Chinese: '单宽流量'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg hydraulics uses 'водно количество' for discharge, not 'дебит'.

translations.km: ល្បឿនហូរតាមឯកតា
translations.my: ယူနစ်ရေထွက်နှုန်း

terms.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
terms.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'.

translations.km: ទំហំថ្មមធ្យម
translations.my: ကျောက်အလယ်အလတ်အရွယ်အစား

terms.context: The spread or uniformity of rock particle sizes. In the Robinson method, gradation is expressed as SD = D84.1/D50. Uniform rock ≈ 1.25; Robinson valid range 1.15–1.47. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the geotechnical/hydraulic engineering term for grain size distribution or grading. Do not translate as 'grade' (implies quality). The symbol 'SD' and ratio notation D84.1/D50 are universal. Spanish/Portuguese: 'granulometría'/'granulometria'. French: 'granulométrie'. Russian/Bulgarian/Serbian: 'гранулометрический состав'. Chinese: '级配'. bg: engineer proposed 'коефициент на едрозърнестост' for the D84.1/D50 gradation SD label (2026-07); applied, but ASK for the standard source — Bulgarian soil mechanics also uses 'коефициент на разнозърненост' for grain-size uniformity.

translations.km: ការចាត់ថ្នាក់ទំហំថ្ម
translations.my: ကျောက်အရွယ်အစားဖြန့်ဝေမှု

terms.context: The fraction of the rock layer volume that is void space (air + water). Default 0.45 for angular crushed rock. Determines how much flow passes through the rock mantle versus over the surface. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator. Distinct from Manning's n (roughness coefficient) — do not confuse the two.
terms.translation_notes: Standard hydraulic/geotechnical term with cognates in most European languages. Always distinguish from Manning 'n' in context — they appear in the same calculator.

translations.km: ភាពប្រហោង
translations.my: အပေါက်ပါမှုနှုန်း

terms.context: Ratio of a material's density to the density of water (dimensionless). Typical crushed granite or basalt ≈ 2.65. Robinson method valid range: 2.54–2.82. Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel calculators.
terms.translation_notes: Use the established civil/geotechnical engineering term meaning 'density relative to water'. Spanish: 'gravedad específica'. French: 'densité relative'. German: 'spezifisches Gewicht'. Arabic: 'الوزن النوعي' is the traditional hydraulic engineering term. Do not use 'unit weight' (weight per volume — has different dimensions).

translations.km: ទំងន់ចំពោះ
translations.my: တိကျသောဆွဲငင်အား

terms.context: Upstream water accumulation at the inlet of a chute or spillway, forming a small pond. In the Robinson method, ponding (Hp > yn) is desirable — the head at the inlet crest acts as a weir, reducing upstream erosion risk. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the irrigation/drainage engineering term for upstream water backing up to form a small beneficial pond at the inlet. Do not use a word implying flooding, failure, or undesirable inundation — ponding here is a design goal. Spanish: 'represamiento'. French: 'mise en charge amont'. Russian: 'подпор воды'. Chinese: '壅水'.

terms.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. H_m = k × v²/(2g). Also called 'minor loss', though in short penstocks these can equal or exceed friction losses. Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.
terms.translation_notes: The term 'minor loss' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'.

terms.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
terms.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. WMO No. 385 entry 1263 gives the full facility names: Spanish 'central hidroeléctrica de pasada', French 'usine hydroélectrique au fil de l'eau', Russian 'русловая гидроэлектростанция' — these are the authoritative terms for the power plant noun. The abbreviated forms 'filo de agua' (es), 'au fil de l'eau' (fr), and 'русловая ГЭС' (ru) are standard in engineering use. German: 'Laufwasserkraftwerk'. Chinese: '径流式水电'.

terms.context: A channel whose cross-section is non-uniform / non-prismatic — a natural or surveyed section defined by station-elevation points, as opposed to a regular trapezoidal shape. Titles the Manning Irregular Channel calculator (mi_) and, in the geometric sense, the Weir Flow Irregular calculator (wi_).
terms.translation_notes: "Irregular" here is GEOMETRIC: the cross-section is non-uniform / natural / arbitrary shape. It is NOT the temporal sense "sporadic / occasional / not-regular" (bg "нередовен" WRONG, uk "нерегулярний" WRONG per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md), and NOT "incorrect / faulty" (ru "неправильное русло" reads as "wrong channel" — prefer "произвольного сечения"). Where the language allows, name the cross-section explicitly ("of irregular cross-section") rather than a bare adjective that could be read as temporal or evaluative.
